extracted.intended_audience: parties to the investigation, interested government agencies, third parties, and other interested persons (i.e., litigants and commenters in ITC Section 337 investigations)
extracted.subtask_description: Instructions and criteria for written submissions to the U.S. International Trade Commission addressing remedy, the public interest, and bonding in Investigation No. 337-TA-1428. Applies to submissions from parties, interested government agencies, and other third parties in response to the Commission's request.

rubrics_metrics.name: Subjects required in written submissions
rubrics_metrics.description: Written submissions must address remedy, the public interest, and bonding in connection with the final disposition of this investigation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Submissions should specifically address the ALJ's recommended determination on remedy and bonding; parties, interested government agencies, and any other interested persons are encouraged to file. Initial submissions are due by close of business on September 22, 2025; reply submissions due by close of business on September 29, 2025.

rubrics_metrics.name: Complainant's required content in initial submission
rubrics_metrics.description: Complainant is requested to identify the remedy sought and to submit proposed remedial orders for the Commission's consideration.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Complainant also is requested to state the dates that the asserted patents expire, to provide the HTSUS subheadings under which the accused products are imported, and to supply identification information for all known importers of the products at issue in this investigation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Form of remedy to be proposed and justified
rubrics_metrics.description: Submissions should address what form of remedy, if any, should be ordered (e.g., exclusion orders, cease and desist orders, LEO, GEO).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If seeking exclusion of an article from entry into the United States for purposes other than entry for consumption, the filer should indicate that and provide information establishing that activities involving other types of entry either are adversely affecting it or likely to do so. The ID recommended a GEO for certain patents and an LEO was requested for others; parties should address or justify alternatives.

rubrics_metrics.name: Public interest factors to address
rubrics_metrics.description: The statute requires consideration of the effects of a remedy upon the public interest.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Commission will consider the effect that an exclusion order would have on: (1) the public health and welfare, (2) competitive conditions in the U.S. economy, (3) U.S. production of articles that are like or directly competitive with those that are subject to investigation, and (4) U.S. consumers. Written submissions are therefore expected to discuss these specific factors in the context of the investigation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Bond amount and justification
rubrics_metrics.description: Submissions should address the amount of the bond that should be imposed if a remedy is ordered.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The ID recommended a bond of 100% of the entered value of the infringing articles during Presidential review and Complainant requested a 100% bond; parties should comment on the appropriate bond amount and provide justification. Note: during the 60-day Presidential review period, subject articles would be entitled to enter the United States under bond in an amount determined by the Commission and prescribed by the Secretary of the Treasury.

rubrics_metrics.name: Who may file and page limits for third parties
rubrics_metrics.description: Parties to the investigation, interested government agencies, and any other interested parties are encouraged to file written submissions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: All submissions from third parties and/or interested government agencies are limited to 10 pages. No further submissions on these issues will be permitted unless otherwise ordered by the Commission.

rubrics_metrics.name: Deadlines and electronic filing requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Timing and manner of filing: initial written submissions must be filed by close of business on September 22, 2025; reply submissions by close of business on September 29, 2025.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Persons filing written submissions must file the original document electronically on or before the deadlines pursuant to 19 CFR 210.4(f). Submissions should refer to the investigation number (Inv. No. 337-TA-1428) in a prominent place on the cover page and/or the first page. See the Commission's Handbook for Electronic Filing Procedures for details.

rubrics_metrics.name: Confidential submissions and redaction procedure
rubrics_metrics.description: Any person desiring to submit a document in confidence must request confidential treatment and mark each document with a header indicating it contains confidential information.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Marking the document with such a header will be deemed to satisfy the request procedure under Rules 201.6(b) and 210.5(e)(2). Documents for which confidential treatment is sought will be treated accordingly. A redacted non-confidential version must also be filed with the Commission and served on any parties to the investigation within two business days of any confidential filing. Non-party confidential comments must be served on the parties pursuant to the applicable Administrative Protective Order.

rubrics_metrics.name: Public availability of non-confidential submissions
rubrics_metrics.description: All nonconfidential written submissions will be available for public inspection on EDIS.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Filing parties should plan redactions and confidential designations accordingly because nonconfidential versions become publicly accessible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reference to governing authority and procedural citations
rubrics_metrics.description: The authority for the Commission's determination is section 337 of the Tariff Act of 1930 (19 U.S.C. 1337) and Part 210 of the Commission's Rules of Practice and Procedure (19 CFR part 210).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Filing and confidentiality procedures reference specific Commission rules (e.g., 19 CFR 210.4(f), 19 CFR 210.13, 19 CFR 201.6(b), 19 CFR 210.5(e)(2)); parties should follow those rules and the Commission's filing handbook.

rubrics_metrics.name: Restriction on additional submissions
rubrics_metrics.description: No further submissions on remedy, public interest, and bonding will be permitted unless otherwise ordered by the Commission.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Parties should therefore include all relevant arguments and evidence in the initial and reply submissions within the stated page limits and deadlines.

rubrics_metrics.name: Identification of investigated articles and import information
rubrics_metrics.description: Submissions (especially Complainant's) should provide identifying information for accused/imported products and importers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specifically requested: HTSUS subheadings for imported accused products and identification information for all known importers; this supports remedy scope, bonding calculations, and public-interest analysis.
